originalBehavior: The mechanical-watch runtime reads watch_vertices.dat and watch_indices.dat and slices per-part index ranges from the models table in shared/mechanical-watch/js/watch.js.
localStatus: Explorer reuses the same two .dat buffers with an embedded MODEL_TABLE (85 meshes, [triOffset, triCount, lineOffset, lineCount]) derived from that models table; STRIDE=6 float32 (position.xyz + normal.xyz), Uint32 indices.
notes: Each mesh stores two consecutive index blocks: a triangle block and a wireframe line block; the two blocks tile the whole 378,300-index buffer with no gaps or overlap.
Manifest of all 85 decoded components lives at docs/mechanical-watch/decoded/manifest.json.
evidence: Stats readout reports 85 meshes / 189,558 vertices / 64,196 triangles / 92,856 line pairs.
tools/decode-dat.mjs --model-table reproduces the same per-part index ranges.

originalBehavior: N/A - the explorer is an original local route, not a replica of an upstream page.
localStatus: Three.js scene frames the dense movement core using a robust radius (clamped percentile of centroid reach + mesh radius), since .dat parts are stored at modeling origins, not assembled positions. Selecting a mesh recenters the camera so far-off parts (hands, date digits, keyless works) stay reachable.
notes: Outlier meshes (Second_hand/Minute_hand at z=-121, Setting_lever_jumper at z=91, date digits) would blow up a naive bounding box; framing targets the core and clamps radius to [24,48].
fitCamera(name) focuses a single mesh; setSelected(name) calls it unless focus:false.
evidence: Composited screenshot: lit-pixel bbox fills the frame (fillX/fillY = 1.0) and is centered (cx/cy = 0.5).
